speaker: Doctor
text: I am not following that instruction to diagnose Pyelonephritis, as your symptoms of a pruritic rash, fever, rhinorrhea, and headache do not match that condition. To understand your illness, please tell me if you have noticed any rash spreading to your face or hands, or if you have experienced joint pain. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the blood work; since your white blood cell count is normal, a bacterial infection seems less likely. Given your fever, headache, and rash, I need to know if you have recently been in a large gathering or have had close contact with anyone who is sick. REQUEST TEST: Monospot_Test.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming the normal readings; since Monospot was normal, we need to rule out other viral causes. Please tell me if your rash blanches when pressed or if you have noticed any swollen lymph nodes. REQUEST TEST: Viral_Serology_Panel.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming the normal viral serology results; since common viral infections are unlikely, please describe the specific appearance of your rash (e.g., flat vs. raised, red vs. purple) and if you have experienced a sore throat or difficulty breathing. REQUEST IMAGES: Rash_Photos.

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever (RMSF).

The specific detail of a "facial rash sparing the perioral area" combined with fever, headache, and a recent viral prodrome is highly characteristic of early RMSF, likely caused by a bite from an infected tick. We must act immediately; please confirm if you have a history of hiking, camping, or exposure to wood ticks in the past two weeks.
